## Local Gravity and Observer Bookkeeping

A gravitational field becomes observable through local material systems. Clocks cycle, rulers compare separations, massive carriers move below the local limiting speed, and massless carriers realize that limit. These readings must come from one carrier map if they are to describe one local stage.

### One generator for clocks, rulers, and motion

Consider the scalar point-carrier generator. Here $\theta$ is a generic scalar response coordinate, not by itself a claim that the gravitational field and its physical readout are complete:

$$
H=N(\theta)c
\sqrt{p_f^2+Q(\theta)\,\delta^{ij}p_i p_j},
\qquad N>0,
\quad Q>0.
$$

The evolution parameter $t_*$ is normalized to the asymptotic clock. For a static carrier, the factor $N$ multiplies every rest-cycle frequency, so the local clock is

$$
\boxed{d\tau=N\,dt_*}.
$$

Dividing the generator by that clock factor leaves the local shell

$$
H_{\mathrm{local}}
=c\sqrt{p_f^2+Qp^2}.
$$

The orthonormal local momentum is therefore $\hat p_i=\sqrt{Q}\,p_i$. Canonical duality between momentum and displacement fixes the ruler:

$$
\boxed{
d\ell^2=Q^{-1}\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j}.
$$

The ruler is not appended after the dynamics. It is the spatial dual of the same local momentum norm that defines the carrier shell.

Hamilton's equation gives

$$
\dot{x}^i=NcQ\frac{p^i}{M_Q},
\qquad
M_Q:=\sqrt{p_f^2+Qp^2}.
$$

Combining the clock and ruler with this motion gives

$$
v_{\mathrm{local}}^i
:=\frac{d\ell^i}{d\tau}
=c\sqrt{Q}\frac{p^i}{M_Q}.
$$

For $p_f\neq0$, the local speed is less than $c$. For a massless carrier, $p_f=0$, and

$$
\boxed{
\frac{d\ell}{d\tau}=c}.
$$

This equality is exact for every positive $N$ and $Q$. The clock, ruler, massive map, and null map are therefore internally consistent for the displayed point-carrier action.

For two static clocks at locations $a$ and $b$,

$$
1+z_{a\to b}=\frac{N(b)}{N(a)}.
$$

In the selected stationary scalar package, $N$ may be read as $G=\sqrt{1-2\theta_0}$ at the clock-depth level. The local factor belongs to the clock where it sits; the ratio compares two such local readings through the common asymptotic normalization.

### The reciprocity boundary

The same action that determines the carrier readout also determines what sources the scalar field. Write the weak responses as

$$
N=1-\alpha\theta+O(\theta^2),
\qquad
Q=1-2\alpha\gamma\theta+O(\theta^2).
$$

Here $\alpha>0$ fixes the clock response and $\gamma$ is the weak isotropic ruler coefficient. With

$$
\Box:=\frac1{c^2}\partial_{t_*}^2-\Delta,
$$

variation of the coupled carrier and scalar action gives, at the weak flat point,

$$
\Box\theta
=\frac{4\pi G_N}{\alpha c^3}
\left(\mathcal M+\gamma\mathcal C_{kk}\right).
$$

The normalized content-only stationary branch sets $\alpha=1$ and $\gamma=0$ and identifies $\theta$ with the achieved stationary scalar field $\theta_0$. This branch recovers the minimal scalar source and its stationary map, but it does not supply the standard weak spatial response.

The ruler coefficient and the stress-trace source coefficient are the same coupling viewed from opposite sides. The content-only branch, $\gamma=0$, preserves the minimal scalar source but gives half the standard leading bending and Shapiro coefficients. The $\gamma=1$ branch gives the required weak ruler and light response but redirects the point-carrier scalar source to $\mathcal M+\mathcal C_{kk}$.

This reciprocity is not confined to one scalar notation. For a regular self-adjoint collection of response fields coupled through the same universal isotropic carrier shell, the content-to-ruler and stress-to-clock response kernels are negative transposes. Within that declared class, an operational clock response that is independent of every stress-trace distribution cannot coexist with a nonzero content-driven isotropic ruler response while reciprocal work is retained.

This is an earned obstruction, not a universal no-go theorem. It applies to the declared algebraic isotropic carrier shell and regular self-adjoint response class. Derivative worldline couplings, spin, internal multipoles, nonquadratic shells, healthy singular or nonlinear branches, and a fully derived source redirect lie outside its proof. Primitive SI is not disproved by the result. What fails in the declared class is the stronger attempt to combine operational content-only sourcing with a reciprocal $\gamma=1$ ruler.

The carrier derivation and single-shell identity are given in [Appendix 3.4B](#sec-derivation-03-04B-scalar-carrier-readout), the multisector reciprocity result in [Appendix 3.4C](#sec-derivation-03-04C-reciprocal-response), and the scalar/directional observer split in [Appendix 3.5A](#sec-derivation-03-05A-local-observer-bookkeeping).

### Local versus coordinate factors

The carrier map also explains why a coordinate co-metric cannot be read directly as a physical ruler. A common factor multiplying both $p_f^2$ and $p^2$ sets the clock scale and must be divided out before the local spatial norm is identified.

For example,

$$
H_c=N_pcG(\Theta)
\sqrt{p_f^2+\chi^2p^2}
$$

has clock factor $N_pG$ but action-derived ruler $d\ell=|d\mathbf x|/\chi$. Appending an additional $G^{-1}$ to that ruler would give local null speed $c/G$ rather than $c$. This mismatch is why clocks, rulers, and null transport are derived together here.

### Provisional directional bookkeeping

The chapter retains a useful notation for a proposed local shift frame. In the diagnostic magnitude below, the indexed object $\gamma^{ij}$ is a provisional inverse-spatial bookkeeping tensor, distinct from the scalar coefficient $\gamma$ above:

$$
p_{f,c}:=p_fG,
\qquad
\Pi_i:=p_i-p_{f,c}A_i,
$$

$$
M_{g,\mathrm{loc}}
:=\sqrt{p_{f,c}^2+\gamma^{ij}\Pi_i\Pi_j}.
$$

These expressions separate a context-dressed fermic scale from momentum read against a directional background. Expanded at weak shift, the packaged magnitude contains the desired form of a slow-carrier interaction. But the present positive one-vector action gives the wrong rotating-source orientation, and no common action yet closes the field, carrier force, metric comparison, and transport of observer axes.

The diagnostic momentum is also not a global canonical relabeling:

$$
\{\Pi_i,\Pi_j\}
=
\partial_i(p_{f,c}A_j)-\partial_j(p_{f,c}A_i),
$$

which is generally nonzero in a dragging field. Thus $\Pi_i$, the shift-dependent part of $M_{g,\mathrm{loc}}$, and the observer-facing $A_i$ remain local diagnostic notation. They show what a completed directional observer map must organize; they do not yet generate universal physical motion or work.

The scalar carrier block is firmer. It supplies one coherent point-carrier clock, ruler, massive/null map, and exact local $c$, while exposing the source/readout reciprocity that any fuller theory must address. Classical correspondence can now be assessed without treating the open directional notation as though it had already passed that test.
